in-place settings fixture, hardlink identity, uninstall/reinstall preservation; GUI not run

notes: All eight payloads installed and selected in an independent temporary Piko root. Existing host software was not taken over.
Installed main executable versions and Windows Authenticode publisher metadata were checked without launching the GUIs.
ToDesk and Sunlogin persistence passed an in-place write, hardlink identity and uninstall/reinstall model test; actual GUI saving remains unverified.
WeChat and Sunlogin use obtainable current official releases; older pinned local releases were not substituted from third-party mirrors. Existing installations were not upgraded.
No actual user PATH/Profile, login credentials, browser/chat data, remote-control services, drivers, startup registrations or default browser settings were changed.

Desktop shortcuts are declarations requiring separate approval. Remote-control services, unattended operation, virtual display/audio/USB drivers and application protocols remain separate acceptance work.

Initial verification inside the active worktree hit Windows EPERM while publishing Orca; the failed staging and logs were preserved privately, and final verification used an independent temporary root.

Windows PowerShell 5.1 metadata verification imports its own Security module explicitly, avoiding an inherited PowerShell 7 module path; no shell installation or host module configuration was changed.
This release adds explicit NSIS file mapping, explicit PE archive resource selection and bounded larger intermediate archives; the final application file limit remains 512 MiB.
PowerShell 7 remains excluded; WPS Office, Annie Office and Perplexity are not added by this change.
